Completeness
World Responsiveness

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Nar.title: Narrative Structure in Worlds
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Nar.content:
Wolf (p.198): narrative is by far the most common structure found in imaginary worlds, and the reason that most of them exist in the first place.
Definitions (Wolf p.199)

Narrative — a series of events which are causally connected
Narrative unit — each event; an actor or agent taking part in an action
Narrative thread — a chain of events revolving around a particular character
Narrative braid — multiple narrative threads that sometimes intersect

Backstory (Wolf p.202)
Backstory is the narrative that happened before the story the audience experiences. It’s one of the primary tools for implying depth — but for us, likely a trap. See Lore as a Trap.
Worldbuilding vs. Narrative Economy
Worldbuilding and storytelling have different relationships with efficiency. Conventional storytelling values economy: include only what advances the story. Experimental narrative often embraces non sequiturs, tangents, and open threads. Worldbuilding of any orientation, however, might value excess: open-ended details can make any world feel developed.
Related

Worldbuilding - Definition and Scope
Lore as a Trap
Catalysts of Speculation
Mark Wolf

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.title: Cultural Invention
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.content:
Wolf calls culture the biggest category of invention — everything made by people: customs, technology, institutions, ideologies, objects, countries (see Wolf’s Taxonomy of Invention).
Le Guin reference: The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas succinctly describes a village’s culture, their beliefs and practices.
This is a rich example with its focu, because the story foregoes traditional storytelling - following a character facing adversity, and witnessing their actions.
Game Examples

Disco Elysium — political factions, failed revolution, class collapse, ideology as character stat.
BioShock — Rapture is an ideology taken to its conclusion; the cultural collapse is readable in rooms, ad, and audio diary.
World of Warcraft — both factions have a fully invented culture embedded in architecture, language, and NPC behavior.
Horizon Zero Dawn — tribal cultures invented as responses to a world; their religion and taboos are a survival logic.

Related

Wolf’s Taxonomy of Invention
World Structure - Wolf’s Eight Elements
Lore as a Trap

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.title: Nature and Invented Physics
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.content:
Wolf’s Nature element (p.155) includes landscape, climate, flora, fauna — and physics. The physical laws of a world are part of its nature.
Most worlds borrow our physics without reference or complication. But the more deliberately a world departs from it, the more it reveals itself as a designed system with a point of view.
For Example: Jumping and Falling in Video Games
We take it for granted that video game players can jump enormous heights and fall even further, particularly in platformers. This stands in contrast to an experience of the real world.
For Example: How Light Works
Electromagnetic principles are a rich target for invention. Change how light behaves and you change:

What organisms can see (visible spectrum, night vision, color perception)
What materials are transparent, opaque, or luminous
What “beauty” looks like — the aesthetic conventions of any culture are downstream of what light does

See also: Teaching the Rules of the World — how games and film transmit world rules to the audience as an experience, but also before the next experience can arrive.
Related

World Structure - Wolf’s Eight Elements
Consistency and Internal Logic
Cultural Invention
Catalysts of Speculation

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.title: Mark Wolf's Taxonomy of Invention
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tax.content:
Invention = the degree to which default assumptions based on the primary (real) world have been changed (Wolf p.34). For example, a green sun is invention. In science fiction, we might want to know the rule behind that invention.  In fantasy, we do not expect to learn it.  Invention is the step from the real world to the fiction world.
Four Types (Wolf p.35)


Nominal — new names for real things. Credits instead of dollars. Realm instead of kingdom. The thing itself doesn’t change; just the term.


Cultural — everything made by people: customs, technology, institutions, ideologies, objects, countries. This is a significant one for creative expression. Deep dive: Cultural Invention.


Natural — different nature.  New landmasses, plants, animals, creatures. Hobbits, sandworms, unicorns. Deep dive: Nature and Invented Physics.


Ontological — parameters of the world’s existence: materiality, laws of physics, space, time. Light speed, time travel, gravity.


Across Genre
Some common reused inventions across many works: elves, clones, laser guns, antigravity (Wolf p.37). Reused across establishes genres.
Related

Worldbuilding - Definition and Scope
Cultural Invention
Nature and Invented Physics
Completeness
Mark Wolf

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tra.title: Transmedia
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Tra.content:
Transmedia describes the phenomenon of multiple stories told in multiple mediums taking place in one world.
Henry Jenkins coined the term “transmedia storytelling” (2003): “a process where integral elements of a fiction get dispersed systematically across multiple delivery channels for the purpose of creating a unified and coordinated entertainment experience.”
Wolf covers transmedia in later chapters — how worlds migrate between media, and how large productions treat world design as an explicit industrial discipline.
Adaptation vs. Transmedia
Adaptation = same story, different medium. The novel becomes a film.
Transmedia = different story, same world. The film exists; the game is set 20 years earlier; the novel explains the villain’s backstory. You don’t need the novel to understand the film, but the novel rewards fans who want more world.
Examples

Star Wars  — films, novels, comics, games, theme parks.
The Matrix — the Animatrix (animated shorts) and Enter the Matrix (game) told stories inaccessible in the films. The Wachowskis designed the transmedia experience as a whole.
Halo  — the novel The Fall of Reach was released before the first game.

Related

Worldbuilding - Definition and Scope
Completeness
Consistency and Internal Logic
Lore as a Trap
Bounded Worlds
Mark Wolf

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Wor.title: World Structure - Wolf's Eight Elements
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/Wor.content:
Wolf (p.154–155): a world needs three foundational structures to exist, plus five more that comprise the world itself.
Three Foundational Structures (p.154)

Space — the physical and geographic extent of the world
Time — the world’s history, its present moment, its temporal logic
Characters — inhabitants who give the world agency and perspective

Five Content Elements (p.155)

Nature — landscape, climate, flora, fauna, physics (see Nature and Invented Physics)
Culture — customs, technology, institutions, objects (see Cultural Invention)
Language — how inhabitants communicate; languages, dialects, naming conventions
Mythology — belief systems, cosmology, religion, founding stories
Philosophy — the world’s underlying values; what it thinks is true

Your project doesn’t need all eight — but knowing which ones you’re leaving out is worth considering.
Related

Worldbuilding - Definition and Scope
Wolf’s Taxonomy of Invention
Cultural Invention
Mark Wolf

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/ind.title: Vocabulary
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/Vocabulary/ind.content:
Mark Wolf’s analytic terms — the language for describing a world: how it holds together, how far it departs from the real, what it’s made of, and how it reaches across media.
Three core properties. A world earns its plausibility — the belief it asks of us — through three qualities working together:

Invention — how far the world departs from the real (the four kinds; folder: + Cultural, Nature)
Completeness — a matter of degree; ancillary detail makes a world feel inhabited, and the gaps it leaves invite speculation
Consistency and Internal Logic — a world need not be realistic, but it must not contradict itself

Structure & reach. What the world is made of and how it travels:

World Structure - Wolf’s Eight Elements — three foundations + five content elements
Narrative Structure in Worlds — how stories sit on top of a world
Transmedia — one world across many works

PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/index.title: Bounded Worlds: The Playable and the Imagined
PBOH/Design/Worldbuilding/index.content:
1. What Is The Bounded Worlds Framework?


                  
                  Bounded Worlds is a game design framework that foregrounds the world as a bounded space — expressive through the world's edge. 
                  
                

Every game design project faces the same challenge: our initial ideas are too large to build.  The Bounded Worlds framework provides a direct response.  It encourages worlds that are expressive through their limits rather than their size.
The Bounded Worlds framework is the worldbuilding companion to the Situated Player Roles: where the player roles turn on what the player does, Bounded Worlds turns on how the world defines its edges.
Because the world has overt limits, the designer can focus on making it consistent, inhabited, and intelligible. Bounded Worlds frames (Brian Upton’s) situations as the essential components of worldbuilding: as the player chooses a path through them, exploration expresses their choices within constraint.
2. Which Boundary Defines My World?


                  
                  Every Bounded World has one of three Boundaries — Finite, Closed, or Threshold. 
                  
                

There are a few ways a Bounded World can treat its edges. Some feel complete in themselves. Some present edges that can be approached but not passed. Others are structured around boundaries the player can cross.
For your Bounded Worlds project, your foundational decision: does the world imply or provide an outside?
If it doesn’t, the world is Finite. If it does, ask whether the player can reach it — an outside implied but withheld is Closed; an edge the player passes through is a Threshold.
Finite
The world presents itself as whole. The player engages entirely within what is present — there is no world outside of what’s playable.


                  
                  Examples 
                  
                


Balance (1989) — the world is the platform and the five characters
Monument Valley (2014) — a set of micro-worlds, each small and finite
Mountain (2014) — you are a mountain
Inscryption (2021) — Act 1: the table, the cabin, the game
12 Minutes (2021) — three rooms, one looping conversation; the world is the apartment.  The world exists for 12 minutes
Thomas Was Alone (2012) — abstract rectangles in an empty field; the puzzle-space is the whole world
Journey (2012) — a single pilgrimage from desert to summit; nothing exists outside the arc
Tetris (1984) — the well and the falling shapes, a closed abstract system
Aesop’s Fables — each fable a tiny self-contained world, complete in a few lines (see The Boy Who Cried Wolf)



-A transition from Finite to Bounded:  Yertle the Turtle (1958) — expanding the boundary
Closed
The player can encounter the edge of the world. The boundary is found during play — the system holds the player within its limits — but cannot be passed.


                  
                  Examples 
                  
                


Escape rooms — sealed by design; the walls hold you for the duration of play
Terrariums, zoos, prisons —  a world inside the world
Disneyland — the berm and landscaping hide the outside world from view; once inside, every sightline stays in-theme
The Exterminating Angel (Luis Buñuel, 1962) - bourgeois characters are stuck in their own world, a house
Dr Langeskov, The Tiger, and The Terribly Cursed Emerald: A Whirlwind Heist - backstage from the real (and inaccessible) game
Return of the Obra Dinn (2018) — the ship is the playable enclosure; ports, empire, weather, and voyage exist as evidence
Papers, Please (2013) — the checkpoint booth holds the player while Arstotzka’s politics press in through papers, guards, news, and family consequences
Tacoma (2017) — the station is explorable, but Earth, corporate power, and the crew’s lives remain outside the accessible corridors, readable only through traces
Gone Home (2013) — the storm-lit house is the world; the family’s wider life is implied through rooms, objects, and absences
BioShock (2007) — Rapture is sealed by the ocean; the surface exists as memory, ideology, and almost-impossible escape
Snowpiercer (Bong Joon-ho, 2013) — the train holds the last of humanity; outside is death, therefore the cars cannot be left
Flatland (Edwin Abbott, 1884) — two-dimensional beings who cannot reach the third dimension they are shown
The Platform (Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia, 2019) — a vertical prison-pit; the structure holds each prisoner to their level
La Maison en Petits Cubes (Kunio Katō, 2008) — a whole life stacked as rooms, read by diving down through them; it would be Finite but for the moment other structures appear in the distance — an outside that plainly exists, and that he never ventures to
P.T. (Kojima Productions, 2014) — an L-shaped corridor that loops on itself; you walk forward but never leave
Slaughterhouse-Five (Kurt Vonnegut, 1969) — Billy Pilgrim is kept in an alien zoo;



Threshold
The player can approach and pass from one state or space into another.


                  
                  Examples 
                  
                


Alice in Wonderland (Lewis Carroll, 1865) — down the rabbit-hole into a world with its own logic
The Matrix (Wachowski Sisters, 1999) — crossing between the simulation and the real
Inception (Christopher Nolan, 2010) — descent through nested dream layers, each a world within a world
Paprika (Satoshi Kon, 2006) — the boundary between dream and waking dissolves
Portal (2007) — the portal itself is the crossing: step through one space, emerge from another
Psychonauts (2005) — you cross from the physical camp into the interior worlds of other minds
World of Tomorrow (Don Hertzfeldt, 2015) — a child pulled across time into a distant, stranger future
Spirited Away (Miyazaki, 2001) — Chihiro passes through the tunnel into the spirit world, before crossing back
Piranesi (Susanna Clarke, 2020) — the labyrinthine house connects to our world through hidden ways
Pan’s Labyrinth (Guillermo del Toro, 2006) — Ofelia moves between wartime Spain and the faun’s underground kingdom
Twin Peaks (1990–1991, 2017) — the town opens onto the Red Room, another order of reality
Severance (2022–) — the threshold splits work-self from home-self; crossing it changes who you are
Hades (2020) — each escape attempt crosses out of the Underworld toward the surface
The Chronicles of Narnia (C.S. Lewis, 1950–1956) — through the wardrobe into Narnia and back again



A Boundary describes the player’s experience of the edge, not a property of the world itself. Judge it from inside the player’s perspective — a locked door only reads as Closed if the player feels it as sealed — not from an outside description of “the thing” (the room, the ship, the pocket dimension). And a Boundary can change over the course of play: a game might hold Closed for its first hour, then open into a Threshold once a door finally gives way. Naming a Boundary describes the experience right now, not a fixed label for the whole game.

3. What Fundamentals Will Shape Your Design?


                  
                  A handful of design concepts shape how the player meets, inhabits, and reads the world. 
                  
                

Meeting the World
How a player first enters a Bounded World is itself a designed moment: reading the boundary, sensing the place, an entry that can carry awe, dread, or curiosity.
Responsiveness
A world feels inhabited when it answers the player with memory, behavior, and consequence; it’s where the concept meets the practical work of building it.
Teaching The Rules
A world that runs on invented rules has to teach them, ideally through low-stakes play rather than a tutorial that pauses to explain.
Catalysts of Speculation
The deliberate gaps the player’s imagination fills
Awkward Exposition
Show don’t tell.
Go Deeper: Wolf’s Vocabulary
Mark Wolf’s Building Imaginary Worlds (the lecture) frames a world through three core properties — invention, completeness (by degree), and consistency — that together earn its plausibility. The gaps left by completeness are what invite the player’s speculation. Find each page:

Consistency and Internal Logic — consistent, not realistic
Completeness — inhabited by degree; the gaps invite speculation
Wolf’s Taxonomy of Invention — four steps away from the real world, deepest in culture and nature
World Structure - Wolf’s Eight Elements — space, time, characters, plus five content elements
Narrative Structure in Worlds — stories sit on top of a world, which can afford excess over economy
Transmedia — one world across many works

Further reading: Emissary’s Guide to Worlding.
4. What Suggestions Will PBOH Offer?


                  
                  PBOH turns your Bounded World into a build plan — a recommended order for making it in a game engine. 
                  
                

Get started using PBOH with your preferred LLM.

PBOH/Design/_References/Comic---Calvin-a.title: Comic - Calvin and Hobbes
PBOH/Design/_References/Comic---Calvin-a.content:
Creator: Bill Watterson | Year: 1985–1995 | Format: Newspaper comic strip
The newspaper comic following six-year-old Calvin and his stuffed tiger Hobbes. The “Spaceman Spiff” strips — Calvin’s imagined fighter-pilot alter ego — are a recurring reference for how graphic design alone (size, bold color, exaggeration, composition, contrast between fantastical and mundane) can evoke a strong emotional reaction.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---2001-A-Sp.title: Film - 2001 A Space Odyssey
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---2001-A-Sp.content:
Director: Stanley Kubrick | Year: 1968
What It Is
A film in three movements: prehistoric humanity encountering a black monolith, a mission to Jupiter aboard a ship with a homicidal AI, and a transcendent final sequence.
www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Annihilat.title: Film - Annihilation
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Annihilat.content:
Director: Alex Garland | Year: 2018
Based on the novel by Jeff VanderMeer (2014)
What It Is
A team of scientists enters Area X — an expanding zone where the rules of biology, identity, and physics have stopped working.
www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Arrival.title: Film - Arrival
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Arrival.content:
Director: Denis Villeneuve · Year: 2016 · based on Ted Chiang’s “Story of Your Life”
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A linguist is brought in to communicate with aliens whose written language has no beginning or end — and learning it begins to reshape how she experiences time. The plot is first contact; the achievement is tone: two hours of slow awe, dread, and grief held in perfect suspension, built from fog, low sound, and patience. A model for how atmosphere can carry meaning that exposition never states.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Balance-(.title: Film - Balance (1989)
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Balance-(.content:
Directors: Christoph & Wolfgang Lauenstein · Year: 1989 · Runtime: 7 min
Academy Award, Best Animated Short (1990)
www.youtube.com/watch
Five identical men stand on a small platform floating in empty space. When any one of them moves, the platform tilts — the others must shift to compensate. They fish over the edge. One pulls up a heavy box that plays music. The struggle to possess it destroys the balance they all depend on, making it a moral tale.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Bardo.title: Film - Bardo
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Bardo.content:
Director: Alejandro G. Iñárritu · Year: 2022 · full title Bardo, False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths
Fame tier: cult-niche (polarizing)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A celebrated Mexican journalist-filmmaker drifts through a limbo built from his own memory and self-doubt — scenes swell into dream sequences (a dance floor, a desert of bodies, a flooded apartment) and bleed into one another without boundaries. Autobiography staged as dream logic; the title’s “bardo” is the Buddhist state between death and rebirth, and the film’s spaces behave accordingly.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Beau-Is-A.title: Film - Beau Is Afraid
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Beau-Is-A.content:
Director: Ari Aster · Year: 2023 · A24
Fame tier: famous (divisive)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A paranoid man tries to get home to his mother, and the world escalates around him in exact proportion to his anxiety — the street outside his apartment is a war zone, strangers’ kindness curdles into captivity, an animated play swallows decades of his life. The environment isn’t distorted by his fear; it is his fear, staged literally. A maximalist example of a world built from one character’s interior state.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Birdman.title: Film - Birdman
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Birdman.content:
Director: Alejandro G. Iñárritu · Year: 2014 · full title Birdman or (The Unexpected Virtue of Ignorance)
Fame tier: famous (Best Picture)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A faded movie star mounts a Broadway comeback, filmed to look like one single continuous shot — the camera prowls through backstage corridors, dressing rooms, rigging, and out onto the stage without ever appearing to cut. The labyrinth of the theatre becomes the inside of his unraveling head, and the unbroken movement means the audience travels the space rather than being shown it. A master reference for continuous presence through connected interiors.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Coraline.title: Film - Coraline
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Coraline.content:
Director: Henry Selick | Year: 2009 | Runtime: 100 min
Based on the novella by Neil Gaiman
Coraline discovers a small door in her new house that leads to an “Other World” — a version of her life in which everything is better and her “Other Mother” is attentive and loving.
The Other World is a Small World built as a lure.  The door is the threshold, and the question of whether Coraline can return through it drives the film.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Don't-Wor.title: Film - Don't Worry Darling
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Don't-Wor.content:
Director: Olivia Wilde · Year: 2022
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
An idyllic 1950s company town — perfect houses, perfect dinners, husbands who drive into the desert each morning to a project no one questions — that begins to crack at the seams for one housewife. The utopia is a constructed reality, and the film’s tension lives in its surfaces: the more flawless the world looks, the more wrong it feels. A clean example of an environment whose perfection is the threat.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Dune.title: Film - Dune
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Dune.content:
Director: Denis Villeneuve | Years: 2021, 2024
Based on the novel by Frank Herbert (1965)
What It Is
The story of Paul Atreides and the desert planet Arrakis — the only source of spice, the most valuable substance in the universe. The world is built from a single ecological fact outward: there is almost no water on Arrakis. Everything else follows from that.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Eraserhea.title: Film - Eraserhead
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Eraserhea.content:
Director: David Lynch · Year: 1977 · black and white
Fame tier: cult-niche (the canonical midnight movie)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A man drifts through a desolate industrial landscape — hissing radiators, droning machinery, corridors of stained concrete — caring for a deformed child in a one-room apartment. Almost nothing is explained and almost nothing happens; the film is carried entirely by its environment and sound design, a sustained atmosphere of industrial dread you inhabit rather than follow. The reference for a world whose texture is the whole experience.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Eternal-S.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Film - Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Eternal-S.title: Film - Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Eternal-S.content:
Director: Michel Gondry · Year: 2004 · Writer: Charlie Kaufman
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A man undergoes a procedure to erase his memories of a failed relationship — and midway through, changes his mind. Most of the film takes place inside the memories as they’re being deleted: he flees with the remembered version of her through collapsing locations, hiding her in memories where she doesn’t belong. Memory as a traversable, crumbling space — rooms losing their walls, faces blurring, a beach house disintegrating around a conversation.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Fight-Clu.title: Film - Fight Club
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Fight-Clu.content:
Director: David Fincher | Year: 1999 | Runtime: 139 min
A film whose late revelation forces the viewer to reinterpret every preceding scene. A canonical case of Revelation and Recontextualization — the twist works because it transforms the characters in our minds, not because of the shock at the moment of reveal.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Get-Out.title: Film - Get Out
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Get-Out.content:
Director: Jordan Peele | Year: 2017 | Runtime: 104 min
A horror-thriller about a Black photographer visiting his white girlfriend’s family. Chris’s small choices — to stay civil, to maintain composure under accumulating pressure — are dilemmas with double impact: they make us feel, and they’re culturally insightful. A central example for Character Dilemmas.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Inception.title: Film - Inception
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Inception.content:
Director: Christopher Nolan | Year: 2010 | Runtime: 148 min
Inception follows a team of thieves who enter people’s dreams to extract or plant information. Dreams are layered — a dream within a dream within a dream — each level with its own spatial logic, time dilation, and rules of physics.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Inside-Ou.title: Film - Inside Out
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Inside-Ou.content:
Director: Pete Docter · Year: 2015 · Pixar
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A girl’s mind rendered as a literal, navigable world: emotions as a control-room crew, memories as glowing orbs in vast shelved canyons, personality as islands that can crumble, a train of thought you can ride. The most thorough mainstream example of building an interior as physical architecture — every space is a metaphor that also works as a place.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---La-Maison.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Film - La Maison en Petits Cubes.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---La-Maison.title: Film - La Maison en Petits Cubes
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---La-Maison.content:
Director: Kunio Katō · Year: 2008 · Runtime: 12 min
Academy Award, Best Animated Short Film (2009)
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
An old widower lives in a town slowly drowning in water; each time the level rises, he builds a new cube of a room on top of his house. When he drops his pipe through the floor hatch, he puts on a diving suit and descends — down through every submerged story of his own home, each level holding the memories of the life he lived there. The house is a vertical archive of a whole life, read from the most recent layer to the oldest.
Watch: www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Lamp-(200.title: Film - Lamp (2002)
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Lamp-(200.content:
Director: Tom Kuntz, Mike Maguire (MJZ) | Year: 2002 | Runtime: 1 min
A short film (originally an IKEA commercial directed by Spike Jonze, but the 2002 Lamp short referenced in lecture is the standalone version of similar form) about a discarded lamp left out in the rain. Its emotional toolkit: cinematography, color, low POV, anthropomorphization, music — and a twist ending that highlights how absurd the manufactured sympathy was. A reference for Designed Experiences.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Lord-of-t.title: Film - Lord of the Rings
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Lord-of-t.content:
Director: Peter Jackson | Years: 2001–2003
Based on the novels by J.R.R. Tolkien (1954–1955)
What It Is
The defining example of modern fantasy worldbuilding. Middle-earth was not invented for the story — Tolkien built the languages first, then the mythology, then the history, then the map. The novels and films came last.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Naked-Lun.title: Film - Naked Lunch
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Naked-Lun.content:
Director: David Cronenberg · Year: 1991 · from William S. Burroughs’s novel
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
An exterminator-turned-writer descends into a hallucinated city where his typewriter is a talking insect, reports are filed to handlers who may not exist, and the writing of the book is the drug experience. Addiction, guilt, and authorship blur into one continuous hallucination — the film never marks where reality ends. A reference for worlds where the protagonist’s creative act and their delusion are the same thing.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Pan's-Lab.title: Film - Pan's Labyrinth
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Pan's-Lab.content:
Director: Guillermo del Toro | Year: 2006 | Runtime: 118 min
Set in post-Civil War Spain, the film follows Ofelia, a young girl who discovers a labyrinth and encounters a faun who claims she is a lost princess. The film holds ambiguity about whether the fantasy world is real or a coping mechanism.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Paprika.title: Film - Paprika
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Paprika.content:
Director: Satoshi Kon | Year: 2006 | Runtime: 90 min
Based on the novel by Yasutaka Tsutsui
A device called the DC Mini allows therapists to enter patients’ dreams. When the device is stolen, dream and reality begin to bleed together.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Poor-Thin.title: Film - Poor Things
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Poor-Thin.content:
Director: Yorgos Lanthimos · Year: 2023 · from Alasdair Gray’s novel
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A woman revived with a new, unformed mind tours a heightened, candy-colored not-quite-Victorian world — Lisbon, a cruise ship, Paris — encountering everything (food, sex, cruelty, philosophy) for the first time, without shame or prior script. The journey structure is the point: each place is a stage of a mind assembling itself, and the stylized world reads as her expanding perception.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Safe.title: Film - Safe
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Safe.content:
Director: Todd Haynes · Year: 1995
Fame tier: cult-niche (Village Voice critics’ best film of the 1990s)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A suburban housewife develops a mysterious illness — perfume, exhaust, her own living room seem to be poisoning her — and the film never confirms whether the cause is environmental or psychological. Shot with clinical wide framing that keeps her small inside immaculate interiors, it builds dread entirely from tone: nothing jumps out, nothing is explained, and the ordinary world simply stops feeling safe. A master class in sustained, sourceless unease.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Severance.title: Film - Severance
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Severance.content:
Creator: Dan Erickson | Year: 2022– | Network: Apple TV+
Severance follows employees at Lumon Industries who have undergone a surgical procedure that divides their memories at the elevator — work-self  knows only the office; home-self knows nothing of work.
Severance literalizes the uncrossable boundary — not as a physical wall but as a neurological divide.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Snowpierc.title: Film - Snowpiercer
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Snowpierc.content:
Director: Bong Joon-ho | Year: 2013 | Runtime: 126 min
Based on the French graphic novel Le Transperceneige
After a climate catastrophe freezes the Earth, all surviving humanity lives on a perpetually moving train circling the globe. The train is the world — its class hierarchy enforced by position in the cars.
The train is a closed system with enforced limits. Moving forward through the cars is the only direction the world allows, and the engine at the front is the uncrossable horizon.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Sophie's-.title: Film - Sophie's Choice
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Sophie's-.content:
Director: Alan J. Pakula | Year: 1982 | Runtime: 150 min
Adapted from William Styron’s novel. The film’s central dilemma is so famous it has entered the language as a phrase. A canonical reference for the idea that the dilemma can be more meaningful than the outcome — and for the way an unwinnable choice transforms a character forever.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Spirited-.title: Film - Spirited Away
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Spirited-.content:
Director: Hayao Miyazaki | Year: 2001 | Studio: Studio Ghibli
What It Is
A young girl falls into the spirit world and must work in a bathhouse to survive and find her way home.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Tango-(19.title: Film - Tango (1981)
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Tango-(19.content:
Director: Zbigniew Rybczyński · Year: 1981 · Runtime: 8 min
Academy Award, Best Animated Short Film (1983)
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A single static shot of one cramped room. A ball bounces in; a boy climbs through the window to fetch it — and his loop repeats. Then another person enters on their own loop, then another, until thirty-six characters from every stage of life are layered into the same space, each repeating their own thread, never colliding. Parallel lives as choreography: one room holding dozens of simultaneous, independent stories.
Watch: www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Cabin.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Film - The Cabinet of Dr Caligari.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Cabin.title: Film - The Cabinet of Dr Caligari
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Cabin.content:
Director: Robert Wiene · Year: 1920 · silent, German Expressionist
Fame tier: famous (the canonical expressionist film)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A hypnotist uses a sleepwalker to commit murders — told through sets that are openly wrong: painted shadows, leaning walls, streets that twist at impossible angles. The world itself is warped to match a narrator’s madness, and the frame story (an early use of the device) reveals the whole tale as a delusion, recoloring everything seen. The original proof that a world’s look can be the inside of a mind.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Fathe.title: Film - The Father
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Fathe.content:
Director: Florian Zeller · Year: 2020 · from his play Le Père
Fame tier: famous (Oscars: Best Actor, Best Adapted Screenplay)
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
Dementia rendered from the inside. An elderly man’s apartment quietly rearranges itself between scenes — furniture moves, rooms merge with his daughter’s flat, the same conversation replays with different faces in the same roles. The audience is never given a stable reality to stand on; the film’s spatial continuity errors are the condition. The strongest example of environment-as-unreliable-narrator.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Matri.title: Film - The Matrix
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Matri.content:
Directors: Lana and Lilly Wachowski | Year: 1999 | Runtime: 136 min
www.youtube.com/watch
The Matrix is a simulated reality maintained by machines to keep humanity docile. The “real world” is a ruined Earth; the Matrix is an earlier era rendered as a simulation. The film’s central drama is the discovery of this boundary, moving between worlds, and achieving control within it.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Other.title: Film - The Others
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Other.content:
Director: Alejandro Amenábar · Year: 2001
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A mother and her two light-sensitive children keep a strict ritual of locked doors and drawn curtains in a fog-bound manor, as unseen intruders seem to move through the rooms. The famous reveal inverts the haunting — recoloring every scene that came before, every noise, every locked door. Underneath the twist: two households occupying the same space without perceiving each other, each experiencing the other as the ghost.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Platf.title: Film - The Platform
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Platf.content:
Director: Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia | Year: 2019 | Runtime: 94 min
In a vertical prison called “the Pit,” inmates occupy numbered levels. Each day a platform descends carrying food — those at the top eat well; those below get whatever remains. Each month, prisoners wake on a different level.
The shaft is the entire world.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Truma.title: Film - The Truman Show
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Truma.content:
Director: Peter Weir · Year: 1998
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A man unknowingly lives his whole life inside a colossal soundstage — his town, his friends, his weather all produced for a broadcast he’s never seen. The world is built specifically to keep one person from leaving it: travel agencies sell fear, roads loop back, and the sea hides the wall. The ending — a sailboat bumping into a painted sky, a staircase, an exit door — is the definitive image of a bounded world and its edge.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Van-(.title: Film - The Van (2019)
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---The-Van-(.content:
Director: Erenik Beqiri | Year: 2019 | Runtime: 15 min | Country: Albania / France
A short Albanian film about two characters facing dilemmas with consequences shaped by their values. A compact reference for narrative arc and Character Dilemmas — the short form makes the little surprises visible.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Twin-Peak.title: Film - Twin Peaks
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---Twin-Peak.content:
Creators: David Lynch and Mark Frost | Year: 1990–1991 (series), 2017 (The Return) | Network: ABC / Showtime
Twin Peaks began as a murder mystery set in a small Pacific Northwest logging town, then expanded into a cosmology involving parallel dimensions, inhabiting spirits, and the Black Lodge — a red-curtained realm operating on its own dream logic.
The Black Lodge is a world with a crossable boundary — characters enter and return changed, or don’t return at all.

PBOH/Design/_References/Film---World-of-.title: Film - World of Tomorrow
PBOH/Design/_References/Film---World-of-.content:
Director: Don Hertzfeldt · Year: 2015 · Runtime: 17 min
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
A 4-year-old named Emily is visited by her adult third-generation clone from the distant future, who takes her on a guided tour through time — memory banks, digital afterlives, dying stars, and a moment when love was copied and stored. Each stop is a minimal, bounded world built from a single memory or idea; the clone narrates with clinical detachment while Emily’s improvised non-sequiturs run underneath. Crayon drawings and flat color carry the full weight of mortality. The reference for the tour structure (guided, passive, revelatory), worlds-as-memories, and devastating minimalism — maximum feeling from almost nothing drawn.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---12-Minute.title: Game - 12 Minutes
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---12-Minute.content:
Developer: Luis Antonio | Year: 2021 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A top-down thriller set entirely in a small apartment. A man returns home to his wife. A cop arrives and kills them both. The loop resets. Everything you know carries over; the apartment doesn’t change.
www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---A-Short-H.title: Game - A Short Hike
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---A-Short-H.content:
Developer: Adam Robinson-Yu (adamgryu) | Year: 2019 | Platform: PC, Switch, consoles
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
A bird named Claire hikes, climbs, and glides up Hawk Peak Provincial Park to find cell reception at the summit. Golden feathers extend your stamina, but nothing rushes you — you can fish, chat with other hikers, race a fox, or just wander the backcountry. Warm, small, and complete in ninety minutes: the reference for a single landscape that makes ascent feel like leisure instead of challenge.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---ABZU.title: Game - ABZU
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---ABZU.content:
Developer: Giant Squid | Year: 2016 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An underwater exploration game with no combat and no fail state — you are a lone diver descending through ocean ecosystems teeming with hundreds of species. You swim, glide, and ride currents; the world answers with schooling fish, shifting light, and the slow reveal of ancient ruins. The story is wordless, told entirely through movement and the places you pass into. Made by the art director of Journey — meditative, painterly, built around awe rather than challenge.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Absolutio.title: Game - Absolution
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Absolutio.content:
Developer: USC student team | Year: 2024 | Platform: PC
A mostly linear visual novel with a distinct presentation and well-placed moments of player choice. Containment of length and mechanics keeps the scope manageable; art, animation, and visual effects do the heavy lifting. A useful 489 reference for what art-and-writing-forward Intermediate projects can look like.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Airplane-.title: Game - Airplane Mode
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Airplane-.content:
Developer: Bacronym | Year: 2020 | Platform: PC
→ Steam
What It Is
A real-time simulation of a six-hour transatlantic flight, played from a coach window seat. There is no goal — you stow your carry-on, flip through the magazine, watch the safety video, fight the seatback entertainment system, doze, and wait out the turbulence. The whole game is the texture of confinement and tedium rendered with obsessive fidelity. A dry, deadpan piece about a mundane space most people share — interactive art made from boredom.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Alan-Wake.title: Game - Alan Wake 2
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Alan-Wake.content:
Developer: Remedy Entertainment | Year: 2023 | Platform: PC (Epic Games Store exclusive — not on Steam), PlayStation, Xbox
Fame tier: famous
→ Wikipedia
What It Is
Two protagonists, two realities: an FBI agent investigates ritual murders in a Pacific Northwest town (crime-board deduction, evidence, place), while the writer Alan Wake is trapped in a Dark Place shaped like a nightmare New York — and can rewrite scenes of the world around him, swapping a location’s reality from inside it. A horror story about authorship where the draft you’re in keeps being revised. Touches all four roles at once — investigation, place and atmosphere, puzzle structure — but it lives deepest in the Dreamer: the world as an expression of a mind writing itself out of the dark.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Alan-Wake.title: Game - Alan Wake
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Alan-Wake.content:
Developer: Remedy Entertainment | Year: 2010 (Remastered 2021) | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A third-person action-thriller set in a dark Pacific Northwest forest. The protagonist is a writer chased by shadowy enemies that can only be hurt after their darkness is burned away with a flashlight. Light is both the navigation tool and the weapon.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Among-Us.title: Game - Among Us
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Among-Us.content:
Developer: Innersloth | Year: 2018 | Platform: PC, mobile, console
→ Steam
A multiplayer social deduction game. Crewmates complete tasks on a spaceship while impostors secretly sabotage and kill. Meetings are called to argue, accuse, and vote. The whole game runs on the tension between hidden information and group judgment.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---An-Airpor.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---An-Airpor.title: Game - An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---An-Airpor.content:
Developer: Strange Scaffold | Year: 2021 | Platform: PC
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person open-world comedy adventure set across airports staffed entirely by dogs. You and your fiancée are the last two humans alive, so you travel — through terminals with functioning flight timetables — chatting with stock-photo dogs, solving their problems, translating alien languages, and catching connections to see her. A walking simulator built on absurdist writing and charm rather than challenge: surreal, warm, and quietly about long-distance love.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Antichamb.title: Game - Antichamber
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Antichamb.content:
Developer: Alexander Bruce | Year: 2013 | Platform: PC
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person puzzle and exploration game set in a seamless, non-Euclidean world. Corridors loop, rooms reconfigure, and ordinary assumptions about direction, distance, and cause and effect repeatedly fail.
Expectation and Payoff
Antichamber uses familiar first-person movement and architectural forms to invite ordinary spatial predictions. A hallway appears to lead somewhere; turning around should return the player to the place they just left; a gap appears impossible to cross.
The world then contradicts those predictions, but each contradiction teaches a usable rule. Surprise becomes a learning rhythm: expectation, violation, reconsideration, and deliberate use. The payoff is not simply that the world is impossible, but that the player gradually learns how to think inside its impossibility.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Assassin'.title: Game - Assassin's Creed II
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Assassin'.content:
Developer: Ubisoft Montreal | Year: 2009 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
Open-world action set in Renaissance Italy. The towers and campaniles of Florence and Venice serve as landmark “weenies” — visible from across the city, climbable, used to reveal the map. A canonical example of Weenies and Landmarks in 3D space.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Baba-Is-Y.title: Game - Baba Is You
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Baba-Is-Y.content:
Developer: Arvi Teikari (Hempuli) · Year: 2019 · Platform: PC, Switch
→ Steam
Puzzle game in which the rules of the world are visible on screen as word blocks — “Baba is You,” “Wall is Stop,” “Flag is Win.” Push the blocks to rewrite the rules, and the world changes accordingly. Move “Win” onto a different object, make walls passable, turn yourself into a rock.
youtu.be/VjqdPjTKPiU

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Back-to-B.title: Game - Back to Bed
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Back-to-B.content:
Developer: Bedtime Digital Games | Year: 2014 | Platform: PC, mobile, console
**→ Steam
What It Is
An isometric puzzle game set inside the dreams of Bob, a chronic sleepwalker. The player controls Subob, Bob’s subconscious guardian — a small dog-like figure — and must guide the oblivious sleepwalking Bob safely back to his bed by placing apples in his path to redirect him around hazards. The world is rendered in a Magritte- and Escher-inflected dreamscape: floating bowler hats, fish, doorways that wrap around the geometry of the level.
youtu.be/7tmOViTk9bY

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Balatro.title: Game - Balatro
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Balatro.content:
Developer: LocalThunk | Year: 2024 | Platform: PC, console, mobile
→ Steam
A poker-roguelike where you build a deck of jokers that interact in escalating combinations. The Amber Acorn boss flips and shuffles all jokers, scrambling the carefully ordered sequences players have built — a small mechanic that creates a memory game on top of an already deep one.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Baldur's-.title: Game - Baldur's Gate 3
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Baldur's-.content:
Developer: Larian Studios | Year: 2023 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A CRPG built on D&D 5th edition rules. Class and ability choices are revisitable at every level-up, giving the player ongoing progression-choice rather than locked-in builds — a contrast with classic class-at-character-creation systems.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---BioShock.title: Game - BioShock
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---BioShock.content:
Developer: Irrational Games | Year: 2007 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person shooter set in Rapture — an underwater city built around Ayn Rand’s philosophy of radical individualism. By the time you arrive, the city has collapsed. You reconstruct what happened through the environment: audio diaries, advertising, architecture, and the behavior of what’s left.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Blue-Prin.title: Game - Blue Prince
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Blue-Prin.content:
Developer: Dogubomb | Year: 2025 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A puzzle game where you inherit a mansion that rebuilds itself each day. At every door you draft a room from three cards, choosing what comes next. The stated goal is to reach Room 46 in 50 draws or fewer.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Breath-of.title: Game - Breath of the Wild
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Breath-of.content:
Developer: Nintendo EPD | Year: 2017 | Platform: Switch, Wii U
→ Nintendo
What It Is
An open-world action-adventure set in a ruined Hyrule a century after Calamity Ganon’s destruction. Link wakes from a hundred-year sleep with no equipment and no map markers, free to approach the world’s challenges in any order. Shrines scattered across the landscape are self-contained puzzle dungeons solved with a small set of physics-based runes — Magnesis (move metal), Stasis (freeze time on objects), Cryonis (raise ice pillars from water), and remote bombs — that recombine across the open world.
youtu.be/kJXwA33c5_Y

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Brothers-.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Brothers-.title: Game - Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Brothers-.content:
Developer: Starbreeze Studios (dir. Josef Fares) | Year: 2013 (Remake 2024 adds local co-op) | Platform: PC, consoles
Fame tier: famous
→ Steam
What It Is
Two brothers journey to fetch a cure for their dying father — and one player controls both at once, one brother per thumbstick. Every puzzle is built on coordinating the pair (the elder boosts, the younger squeezes through bars), so the control scheme quietly becomes the relationship. The famous final beat works because of the controls, not despite them — the single strongest example of a control scheme as the story’s meaning. The 2024 remake adds two-player co-op, one brother each.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Catacombs.title: Game - Catacombs of Solaris
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Catacombs.content:
Developer: Ian MacLarty | Year: 2016 (Revisited 2021) | Platform: PC
→ Steam
An impressionist first-person maze. The walls of the labyrinth are painted with broad, painterly textures that flatten and warp as you move — a Lost Woods rendered as a moving painting.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Children-.title: Game - Children of the Sun
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Children-.content:
Developer: René Rother, published by Devolver Digital | Year: 2024 | Platform: PC
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Steam
What It Is
A sniper with one bullet per level — but the bullet can be re-aimed at the moment of each impact, so a whole compound of cultists becomes a single ballistic puzzle: plan the chain, fire once, steer the kill from head to head. Grimy, hallucinatory styling over a mechanic of total precision. The reference for one constrained verb (a single shot) generating an entire puzzle language.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Cocoon.title: Game - Cocoon
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Cocoon.content:
Developer: Geometric Interactive (dir. Jeppe Carlsen, lead designer of Limbo/Inside) | Year: 2023 | Platform: PC, consoles
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
A small beetle carries entire worlds as glowing orbs on its back — and can dive into any orb, or carry one orb inside another. Every puzzle is built from that single nested-worlds rule, taught wordlessly and escalated with immaculate clarity until you’re juggling realities like keys. The reference for worlds-within-worlds as a playable structure rather than a story conceit.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Creaks.title: Game - Creaks
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Creaks.content:
Developer: Amanita Design | Year: 2020 | Platform: PC, console, mobile
→ Steam
What It Is
A hand-painted puzzle adventure set in a strange mansion you discover by descending into it. The house is inhabited by creatures that turn into furniture under light. Each room is a small puzzle and a small disclosure.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Crimson-D.title: Game - Crimson Desert
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Crimson-D.content:
Developer: Pearl Abyss | Year: 2026 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An open-world action-adventure set in the medieval continent of Pywel. Combat and narrative are peppered in the larger thread - exploring a vast world - sometimes - for its own sake.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Cyberpunk.title: Game - Cyberpunk 2077
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Cyberpunk.content:
Developer: CD Projekt Red | Year: 2020 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An open-world RPG set in Night City, a hyper-corporate megalopolis on the California coast. Based on the tabletop RPG Cyberpunk by Mike Pondsmith.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Death-Str.title: Game - Death Stranding
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Death-Str.content:
Developer: Kojima Productions | Year: 2019 | Platform: PC (Director’s Cut), PlayStation
Fame tier: famous
→ Steam
What It Is
A porter carries cargo across a depopulated, post-apocalyptic America on foot — and the walking itself is the game: weight distribution, balance on scree, river crossings, rope and ladder placement. Other players’ structures appear in your world (bridges, paths, warnings), so the land slowly fills with anonymous mutual aid. The definitive case that traversal — terrain, weight, exhaustion, route-planning — can carry an entire AAA game.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Disco-Ely.title: Game - Disco Elysium
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Disco-Ely.content:
Developer: ZA/UM | Year: 2019 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An RPG set in a city recovering from a failed communist revolution. You play a detective with amnesia. Revachol is a compelling example of cultural invention in games.
youtu.be/6aL7hK8h3WQ

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Dr-Langes.title: Game - Dr Langeskov
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Dr-Langes.content:
Dr Langeskov, The Tiger, and The Terribly Cursed Emerald: A Whirlwind Heist is a short first-person game by Crows Crows Crows (William Pugh, co-creator of The Stanley Parable), released in 2015.
www.youtube.com/watch
Steam
Summary
You arrive expecting to play through a heist adventure — but the game isn’t ready. Instead of starring in the heist, you’re pulled backstage and asked to help run it for someone else. A frantic narrator (voiced by Simon Amstell) guides you through behind-the-scenes tasks: operating stage lights, releasing a tiger on cue, triggering sound effects. The “real” game is always happening just on the other side of the walls, and you’re the stagehand keeping it going.
The joke — and the insight — is that the backstage is the game. There is no actual heist happening on the other side. The player cannot cross the world’s boundary.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Elden-Rin.title: Game - Elden Ring
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Elden-Rin.content:
Developer: FromSoftware | Year: 2022 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An open-world action RPG set in the Lands Between — a dying kingdom whose civilization collapsed after a catastrophic event called the Shattering.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Everybody.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - Everybody's Gone to the Rapture.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Everybody.title: Game - Everybody's Gone to the Rapture
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Everybody.content:
Developer: The Chinese Room | Year: 2015 | Platform: PC, PlayStation
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
An English village, golden-hour and utterly empty, in the minutes after an apocalypse no one witnessed. The vanished residents persist as drifting traces of light that replay fragments of their last conversations — you wander lanes, pubs, and farms, tuning into these echoes to piece together what came for the village and what it meant to each person. BAFTA-winning score. The reference for reconstructing a community (not just a household) from an emptied space.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Everythin.title: Game - Everything (David OReilly)
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Everythin.content:
Developer: David OReilly | Year: 2017 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
You can become anything — an animal, a rock, a galaxy, a blade of grass. Scale is infinite in both directions.
www.youtube.com/watch
Notes for Class
Useful for Week 5 (physical world / observer’s position). The question it raises: if you can be anything, is there a “world” at all, or just a collection of perspectives?

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Fallout-4.title: Game - Fallout 4
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Fallout-4.content:
Developer: Bethesda Game Studios | Year: 2015 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A post-apocalyptic open-world RPG. Its procedural rhetoric: the world is divided into civilization and wilderness, civilization is precious and fragile, the wilderness is hostile but should be looted, violence is usually the answer. Dogs are great.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Firewatch.title: Game - Firewatch
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Firewatch.content:
Developer: Campo Santo | Year: 2016 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person mystery set in the Wyoming wilderness. You’re a fire lookout. Your only contact is a voice on a radio. The wilderness is vast, layered, specific.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---God-of-Wa.title: Game - God of War
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---God-of-Wa.content:
Developer: Santa Monica Studio | Year: 2018 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A reboot of the action series, recast in Norse mythology. The Leviathan Axe gains skills and mechanics through XP progression — the unlocks themselves are a major source of anticipation.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Gone-Home.title: Game - Gone Home
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Gone-Home.content:
Developer: The Fullbright Company
→ Steam
Year: 2013
Platform: PC
Fame tier: successful indie
A first-person exploration game with no combat, no puzzle-solving — just a house to explore and a story to reconstruct. You return to your family’s home to find it empty. Every room is a scene left mid-action. The story of what happened is assembled entirely through objects, notes, and environmental detail.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Gris.title: Game - Gris
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Gris.content:
Developer: Nomada Studio | Year: 2018 | Platform: PC, Switch, PlayStation, Xbox, mobile
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
A wordless platformer about grief, played as a young woman moving through a watercolor world that has lost its color. Each stage of the journey returns one color and one ability — her dress hardens to stone, becomes a glider — and each new ability literally re-colors and reopens the world. No death, no failure, no danger: the entire design question is how to make an emotional progression playable.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Hades.title: Game - Hades
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Hades.content:
Developer: Supergiant Games | Year: 2020 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An action roguelike set in the Greek underworld. You play Zagreus, son of Hades, trying to escape. The underworld is the boundary — leaving it is the entire premise of the game. Every run ends in return.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Her-Story.title: Game - Her Story
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Her-Story.content:
Developer: Sam Barlow
→ Steam
Year: 2015
Platform: PC, iOS
Fame tier: successful indie
A database investigation game with no physical world to explore. The player searches a police archive of video clips — interviews recorded across multiple sessions — by typing keywords. Each search surfaces fragments; contradictions accumulate. The full story emerges  through the player’s own inference.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Horizon-Z.title: Game - Horizon Zero Dawn
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Horizon-Z.content:
Developer: Guerrilla Games | Year: 2017 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
An open-world action RPG set in a far future where tribal societies have formed around the ruins of a technological civilization they no longer understand. Machines roam the landscape. The tribes have built religions and cultures around them without knowing what they are.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Humanity.title: Game - Humanity
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Humanity.content:
Developer: tha ltd. (dir. Yugo Nakamura) / Enhance | Year: 2023 | Platform: PC, PlayStation (VR optional)
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
You are a shiba inu directing endless marching crowds of people — placing commands (turn, jump, float, climb) on the ground to route a river of humanity to salvation, Lemmings-style, across 90 stages. The crowds are both puzzle material and image: masses of identical figures pouring through brutalist white spaces, beautiful and unsettling at once. Mass behavior as mechanic and as metaphor.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---I-Am-Brea.title: Game - I Am Bread
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---I-Am-Brea.content:
Developer: Bossa Studios | Year: 2015 | Platform: PC, consoles, mobile
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Steam
What It Is
You are a slice of bread, and your goal is to become toast. Each corner of the slice grips with a separate input, so movement is a deliberate, hilarious struggle — flopping end over end across kitchen counters toward anything hot enough, while staying edible. Comic physics embodiment: the entire game is the gap between a simple intention and an unruly body.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Indiana-J.title: Game - Indiana Jones 2024
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Indiana-J.content:
Developer: MachineGames | Year: 2024 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A first-person immersive sim built around Indiana Jones. Inherits much of the puzzle / mystery / exploration vocabulary that interactive fiction developed decades earlier.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Inscrypti.title: Game - Inscryption
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Inscrypti.content:
Developer: Daniel Mullins | Year: 2021 | Platform: PC
→ Steam
What It Is
A deck-building roguelike that is also a meta-horror game about the nature of games themselves. The player is trapped playing a card game with a mysterious figure.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Inside.title: Game - Inside
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Inside.content:
Developer: Playdead | Year: 2016 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A side-scrolling puzzle-platformer with no UI, no dialogue, and no stated goal. A boy runs through a bleak, industrial world — sneaking past search parties, wading through flooded facilities, moving among people who no longer act like people. Nothing is explained. No institution is named, no reason given for what he’s fleeing or where he’s headed; the world withholds its own why. What’s happening, and what it means, comes entirely from environment, staging, and what you’re made to do to survive each room.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Journey.title: Game - Journey
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Journey.content:
Developer: thatgamecompany | Year: 2012 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A third-person traversal game built around a single goal: the mountain on the horizon. The mountain is a weenie at planetary scale — visible from the opening shot, always present, the gravitational center of the whole experience.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---KID-A-MNE.title: Game - KID A MNESIA Exhibition
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---KID-A-MNE.content:
Developer: Radiohead × Namethemachine | Year: 2021 | Platform: PC, PS5, macOS
→ Epic Games Store
What It Is
Made in Unreal Engine, a free interactive exhibition that walks through dreamlike rooms built from the artwork, lyrics, and music of Radiohead’s Kid A and Amnesiac.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Kentucky-.title: Game - Kentucky Route Zero
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Kentucky-.content:
Developer: Cardboard Computer | Year: 2013–2020 (five acts) | Platform: PC, consoles
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
A magical-realist adventure in five acts: a truck driver making one last delivery searches for the Zero, a secret highway beneath Kentucky, gathering a caravan of debt-haunted strangers. Scenes are passed through rather than solved — dialogue choices shape tone and memory, not outcomes — and the world (a distillery staffed by skeletons, a museum of dwellings, an underground river) runs on dream logic grounded in real economic grief. The reference for atmosphere-first, theatrical staging in games.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Knights-o.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - Knights of the Old Republic.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Knights-o.title: Game - Knights of the Old Republic
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Knights-o.content:
Developer: BioWare | Year: 2003 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A Star Wars CRPG built around a light-side / dark-side alignment meter. Every dialogue and action choice nudges the bar in one direction, and that aggregate determines what the world looks like and how it ends. A clean example of procedural rhetoric: the game has a strong implicit theory about morality as a one-dimensional axis.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---LA-Noire.title: Game - LA Noire
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---LA-Noire.content:
Developer: Team Bondi / Rockstar Games | Year: 2011 | Platform: PC, consoles | full title L.A. Noire
Fame tier: famous
→ Steam
What It Is
A detective procedural in meticulously rebuilt 1947 Los Angeles: walk crime scenes for physical evidence, then sit suspects down and read their faces — the era-defining facial capture exists so you can judge, line by line, whether a witness is lying. Cases climb from traffic desk to homicide as the city’s postwar glamour rots underneath. The big-budget reference for evidence-gathering and interrogation as core verbs.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Link's-Aw.title: Game - Link's Awakening
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Link's-Aw.content:
Developer: Nintendo | Year: 1993 (remake 2019) | Platform: Game Boy, Switch
A top-down Zelda set on Koholint Island. The hookshot — a quasi-grappling-hook ability — is a canonical “key that is an ability”: once Link has it, previously inaccessible spaces (like the bridge at the start of the demo) open up.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Little-Ni.title: Game - Little Nightmares
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Little-Ni.content:
Developer: Tarsier Studios | Year: 2017 | Platform: PC, consoles
Fame tier: famous
→ Steam
What It Is
A tiny child in a yellow raincoat sneaks, climbs, and hides through the Maw — a vast iron vessel of grotesque adults rendered at dollhouse scale, where furniture is terrain and a kitchen is a level. Physical puzzles and stealth inside a strictly bounded world, with horror built from scale: everything ordinary is enormous, and being small is the mechanic.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Mango-Goe.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - Mango Goes to Mewsic School.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Mango-Goe.title: Game - Mango Goes to Mewsic School
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Mango-Goe.content:
Developer: USC student team | Year: 2023 | Platform: PC
A 489 project that won the Diversity in Video Games Competition at the Congressional Black Caucus’ 2023 Legislative Conference. Considerably more expansive and polished than most Intermediate projects — close to the upper limit of what a semester can produce. If you’re imagining something more ambitious than this, scale back.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Manifold-.title: Game - Manifold Garden
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Manifold-.content:
Developer: William Chyr Studio | Year: 2019 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A first-person puzzle game set in an Escher-style infinite architectural space. Architectural detail does triple duty: it orients the player in a disorienting space, conveys object scale and distance, and creates navigation challenges. A reference case for Reusing Objects and Spaces.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Monopoly.title: Game - Monopoly
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Monopoly.content:
Designer: Lizzie Magie / Parker Brothers | Year: 1935 (current form) | Platform: Tabletop
The canonical American board game. Its procedural rhetoric: get as much money as you can; ownership and investment beat working; collect rent (good) instead of paying rent (bad); luck and persistence are rewarded; if you’re wealthy, jail is just an inconvenience. Originally designed as a critique of land monopoly; the irony is that nearly no one notices.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Monument-.title: Game - Monument Valley
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Monument-.content:
Developer: Ustwo Games | Year: 2014 | Platform: Mobile
→ App Store
What It Is
A puzzle game in which you guide a small princess through impossible architecture.  Inspired by M.C. Escher.
www.youtube.com/watch

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Mountain.title: Game - Mountain
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Mountain.content:
Developer: David OReilly · Year: 2014 · Platform: PC ·
→ Steam
The world is the mountain. There is no outside, no objective, no story.
youtu.be/JND7BRiBvS0

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Naissance.title: Game - NaissanceE
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Naissance.content:
Developer: Limasse Five | Year: 2014 | Platform: PC
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person descent through a gigantic, abstract megastructure — endless concrete halls, shafts of light, geometry that shifts as you pass — with no story, no guidance, and no explanation of what the structure is. The design goal, in the developer’s words, is to make the player feel lost and small inside an unknown universe, and marveled by it. The reference for monumental architecture as the entire experience.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Ocarina-o.title: Game - Ocarina of Time
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Ocarina-o.content:
Developer: Nintendo EAD | Year: 1998 | Platform: N64, GameCube, 3DS
The defining 3D Zelda. The Lost Woods aren’t a maze — they’re a guided experience: the game tells the player what to pay attention to (a musical cue at each fork), and that attention guides them through. You can brute-force it, but you don’t have to.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Octodad.title: Game - Octodad
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Octodad.content:
Developer: Young Horses | Year: 2014 | Platform: PC, consoles | full title Octodad: Dadliest Catch
Fame tier: successful indie
→ Steam
What It Is
You are an octopus in a suit passing as a suburban father, and the controls are deliberately unruly — each flailing limb steered separately through mundane tasks like mowing the lawn and grocery shopping, without arousing suspicion. The comedy is the body, but the heart is the premise: a game about hiding what you are from the people you love, told entirely through how hard it is to walk.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Old-Skies.title: Game - Old Skies
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Old-Skies.content:
Developer: Wadjet Eye Games | Year: 2025 | Platform: PC
→ Steam
A 2D point-and-click adventure about time-travel tourism. A modern descendant of the parser-based and graphic adventure traditions of the 1980s and 90s — same vocabulary, modern interface.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Ori-and-t.filePath: PBOH/Design/_References/Game - Ori and the Blind Forest.md
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Ori-and-t.title: Game - Ori and the Blind Forest
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Ori-and-t.content:
Developer: Moon Studios | Year: 2015 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
A 2D metroidvania built around movement abilities. The double-jump is a classic “key that is an ability” — gaining it transforms which parts of the map you can reach without any new object having entered the world.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Outer-Wil.title: Game - Outer Wilds
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Outer-Wil.content:
Developer: Mobius Digital | Year: 2019 | Platform: PC, console
→ Steam
What It Is
A space exploration game set in a solar system frozen in a 22-minute loop. A civilization died here before you arrived. You piece together what happened by exploring their ruins, translating their writing, following their logic.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Overwatch.title: Game - Overwatch 2
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---Overwatch.content:
Developer: Blizzard | Year: 2022 | Platform: PC, console
→ Battle.net
A team-based first-person shooter with distinct hero abilities. The Lijiang Tower map uses its central tower as a landmark, an objective, and a vertical play surface all at once — a multi-purpose space that lets each hero use it differently.

PBOH/Design/_References/Game---POOLS.title: Game - POOLS
PBOH/Design/_References/Game---POOLS.content:
Developer: Tensori | Year: 2024 | Platform: PC (Windows, macOS, Linux), VR optional
Fame tier: cult-niche
→ Steam
What It Is
A first-person walk through vast, drained and half-flooded pool complexes — tiled corridors, filtration rooms, diving wells, and stairwells that keep going. Six chapters, ten to thirty minutes each. There is no combat, no inventory, no UI, no dialogue, and no music: only footsteps, water, and room tone. The developers describe it as being “like an art gallery where you look around and listen to the sounds,” and are explicit that “there are no monsters chasing you or jumping suddenly towards you, but the game can feel oppressive.”
It is the purest game-length expression of the Backrooms liminal-space aesthetic: a built environment emptied of people and purpose, still lit and still humming, whose scale and repetition do all the work that a monster would do elsewhere.
Why It’s Useful Here
It separates dread from threat. Almost every horror game teaches that tension comes from something that can hurt you. POOLS removes the thing entirely and keeps the tension, which makes it unusually good evidence when a student assumes atmosphere requires a pursuer.
Its boundary is Closed. The complex is enormous and keeps unfolding, but the player never reaches an outside — no exterior, no sky, no other people. The edge is felt as more building, not as a wall.
It is a network labyrinth. Rooms connect to rooms with no branching tree to solve and no center to reach; you keep moving and the space keeps continuing. Compare the unicursal and multicursal cases — here the illusion of freedom comes from sheer extent.
